concerns.text: FR-005 mandates a 'paired t-test' for statistical significance. The tasks (T031) implement 'McNemar's test' instead. While the plan notes this as a spec conflict, the tasks do not provide a task to update the spec or formally document the deviation in the codebase (e.g., a migration note or updated requirement ID). The implementer has no task to reconcile this requirement mismatch.

FR-007 mandates a 'post-hoc power analysis'. Tasks (T032) implement 'A priori power analysis'. Similar to FR-005, there is no task assigned to update the spec requirement or document the rationale for this methodological shift in the implementation artifacts, leaving the spec requirement unaddressed in the task list.

FR-002 mandates an 'encoder-only' language model (e.g., DistilBERT). Tasks (T019) implement 'T5-small (Encoder-Decoder)'. This is a fundamental architectural deviation. There is no task to update FR-002 or create a new requirement ID reflecting the T5 architecture, meaning the current spec requirement is technically unfulfillable by the planned tasks.

The spec assumes 'at least 5,000 valid trajectories'. Tasks (T016) treat this as '[deferred]' and T026 dynamically determines N based on power analysis. There is no task to handle the specific scenario where the assumption fails (e., if <5,000 triples are found) other than a generic 'report shortage'. The spec requires a specific fallback strategy for this assumption failure which is not explicitly tasked.

SC-006 defines 'Statistical Power' measurement against a 'paired t-test'. Since the tasks implement McNemar's test (T031), the success criterion SC-006 is technically unmeasurable against the implemented method. There is no task to update SC-006 to reference McNemar's test or the new statistical method.

Task T026 references 'androidworld' dataset with DOI '10.48550/arXiv.2405.14793'. While the DOI is present, the task description does not explicitly link this to the 'Verified Datasets' block or a specific contract schema for the evaluation set, potentially violating Constitution Principle II if the citation isn't formally resolved in the code.
